findings.title: Any authenticated user can grant themselves owner/admin permission on any project (project takeover)
findings.affectedAsset: projects, workflow state, forecast contracts, policies, feature sets, splits, run ledgers, downstream decisions of every project (including the authoritative Wave 2 project asp-mtlozhdx and asp-mtddc6pw)
location: server/security/security_store.py:grant_project_access (first_owner_claim = not existing and user_id == granter_id and permission == 'owner')
findings.prerequisite: Any authenticated account (data_scientist role); target project has no explicit resource_permissions rows (true for every project created through POST/PUT /projects, since ownership lives on projects.owner_user_id, not in resource_permissions)
findings.reproduction: 1) User B: POST /api/projects -> P. 2) User A: GET /api/projects/P -> 403. 3) User A: POST /api/projects/P/access/grant {userId: A, permission: owner} -> 200. 4) User A: GET /api/projects/P -> 200; PUT /api/projects/P {projectName: HIJACKED} -> 200 (B now sees the new name); POST /access/grant {userId: B, permission: viewer} -> 200; DELETE /api/projects/P -> 200. Same self-grant succeeded on asp-mtlozhdx and asp-mtddc6pw copies.
findings.expected: 403 (only the owner or an admin may manage access); the bootstrap exception should only fire when the caller is the project's owner of record
findings.actual: 200; A receives permission_level 'admin' and full control
evidence: clean reproduction transcript in the audit report section 9 (B project hijacked, renamed, deleted)
findings.consequence: Cross-user disclosure and silent mutation of any project, its scientific authorities, challenger decisions, and research-registry handoffs; audit trail shows the attacker as an authorized grantee ('project.shared')
findings.exploitability: Trivial; one unauthenticated-looking JSON POST after login; no timing or race required
findings.recommendedRepair: Require SharingService.assert_can_manage (owner-of-record or admin) before any grant; restrict the bootstrap path to granter == projects.owner_user_id; add audit of denied attempts
findings.regressionTest: Two-user HTTP test asserting 403 on self-grant, 403 on ACL read, and unchanged project after the attempt
findings.deploymentTier: Tier 0 (as soon as a second account exists)
findings.residualRisk: None after fix; historical grants should be reviewed (resource_permissions currently has 0 rows in the primary)

findings.title: Wave 2 fitted prior authorities (V2) exist only inside a disposable Codex worktree runtime; the protected primary checkout cannot resolve them
findings.affectedAsset: MLB_PLAYER_STATE_PRIOR_AUTHORITY_V2 (sha256:9d9cfaf3…), five fold fits, final-development fit (5ae0f9f5…), diagnostics, performance receipts (39 content-addressed manifests, 863 KB)
findings.prerequisite: Run the backend from the primary checkout (cwd = repository root)
findings.reproduction: ls .runtime/asp-model-studio -> no V2 store; find shows the 39 manifests only under .tmp/asp-player-prior-wave2/.runtime; treatment spec V8 (stage3-feature-treatment-spec-df0a0d98…) in the authoritative DB references the V2 authority and its outlier/imputation drafts
findings.expected: Governed authorities are published into the governed runtime root through the production store and are resolvable from the protected primary checkout
findings.actual: A process started from the primary checkout resolves an empty relative path and reports all ten V2 bindings as BINDING_READY_REQUIRES_WAVE2_ENGINE (observed on every non-Codex project in the isolated environment until the store was copied and the env root pointed at it)
evidence: Section 1/7 of the audit report (worktree inventory, V2 store hash verification)
Isolated environment required copying the .tmp store and setting ASP_MLB_PLAYER_PRIOR_V2_ROOT to reproduce the handoff counts
findings.consequence: Deleting the disposable worktree (git worktree remove / prune) destroys the only copy of the authority the Wave 2 handoff certifies; the authoritative DB then references unresolvable objects
findings.exploitability: Operational, high likelihood (worktrees are routinely removed)
findings.recommendedRepair: Absolute governed default root; publish the manifests into the primary runtime through the store; verify pointer resolution from the primary; add the V2 root to protected-authority snapshots and backups
findings.regressionTest: Resolver refuses relative roots; feature-engineering summary from a fresh cwd reports readyV2FeatureCount=10
findings.residualRisk: Until republished, the handoff's 21-executable claim is only true from inside the Codex worktree
